name: weak-isospin-t3-grading
description: Weak-isospin T3 = sign(writhe)/2 grading orthogonal to the generation winding n. Resolves the winding_content_not_injective degeneracy (charm n=5 = strange n=5) named by the meson-fluxtube audit (qou-qpj9). T3 is the sign-half of the signed writhe kappa = +-n whose magnitude is the generation. Gell-Mann-Nishijima Q = T3 + Y/2 is a checked theorem (derive-then-check), not a fit. All facts proved in Lean, sorry-free.

derivation.object: signedWrithe kappa : Quark -> Z  (= +-n, the net signed crossing of the canonical T(2,n)=sigma_1^{+-n} braid)
derivation.orthogonality: sign(kappa) and |kappa| are independent data of the integer kappa; T3 (sign) is orthogonal to generation (magnitude) by construction
derivation.sign_convention: up-type = positive crossing, inherited from the strong-isospin bowtie_K orientation (pp = sigma_g positive, nn = sigma_g^-1)

open_remainder.open_1: the sign is FORCED by the bowtie_K orientation (not merely consistent) — physical openness, decidable over the finite toy
open_remainder.open_2: lift of the Z/2 to the SU(2)_L gauge action on H_n(q) reps; combined with the generation tower reproduces quark masses / CKM

anti_fit_statement: T3 = sign(signedWrithe)/2 is defined from topology; GMN is a checked theorem, not a definition. The one convention (up=positive) is inherited from the existing corpus bowtie_K datum. The open primary is a content-bearing class with NO instance; no anchor-inverted grading wired to production.
